quest.title: Villains
quest.description: In the sparsely populated wilderness, you suddenly heard strange arguing sounds...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x350, Primogem x40, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x5, Paimon's "Food Fund" x1, Formula: "Pure Water" x1

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: Hand your brother over! That heartless rat's betrayed us — the boss is practically frothing at the mouth!

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: H—How's that possible!? I thought you were all friends?

dialogues.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
dialogues.text: It's precisely because we were friends that he could betray us, Blanche. This is how the world works.

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: But... I don't know where he is either...

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: "I don't know either"? You really are Ley Lines... absolutely Ley Lines!

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: Ley Lines...?

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: Outdated! Ley Lines are outdated! Ley Lines shall be abandoned! The future belongs to the New Tide!

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: I... I... I don't know what you're talking about, but if he did something wrong... let me apologize on his behalf... Just please let me go...

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: Alright, sure. Let's take a vote.

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: Take a vote... on what?

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: Whether or not we should let you go, of course. Do you think the New Tide revolves around you?

dialogues.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
dialogues.text: That's right. A vote is necessary when opinions differ. Making arbitrary demands won't cut it. This is also how the world works, Blanche.

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: W—Wait!

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: Wait for what? You're gonna vote for letting the guy go, right? Fine. Let's make it one to zero in your favor.

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: But the New Tide commands me otherwise. Now it's a one-one draw.

dialogues.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
dialogues.text: Staying loyal to your friends is also how the world works. Sorry, Blanche. I'm with the New Tide on this one.

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: One to two! What an extraordinary twist of fate!

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: You... scoundrels! I haven't agreed to anything!

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: Try to understand the situation, would you, girl? You're just one, and guess what? One is completely useless when it's two against one!

dialogues.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
dialogues.text: Yup. The principle of "majority rules" is not only how the world works, but also a fundamental part of "order."

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: Now, you better spit it out! Where is the traitor hiding?!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do I get a vote?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And Paimon, too!

dialogues.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
dialogues.text: Oh? Hey there, friends. What a coincidence that we should meet here in the wilderness. So, how will you be voting?

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: Hey, wait! Who are you two? Don't act like we're friends. Has no one taught you the most important thing is keeping a respectful distance from other people?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're one to talk about keeping distance, when you're the ones bothering others! You've got some nerve!

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: Hey, calm down, little one. Y'know what, it's pretty cool how you're just floating around! Why not work under me? I'll call you the Trendy Flyer!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No way! Paimon's friend is way cooler than you... Hey! You're messing Paimon's train of thought up! Let the kid go right this second!

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: Haha! You're not part of my gang, so why should I listen to you?

dialogues.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
dialogues.text: That said, it's two to two now... somehow.

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: Hey, Wolfhook, what are you doing, accepting votes from people we don't even know?

choices.text: Where's the voting button? Someone help me vote for letting the kid go.

response.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
response.text: Now it's two to three. Another extraordinary twist of fate.

response.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
response.text: Stop, Wolfhook! I thought we were friends! Which side are you on?

choices.text: On the side of majority rule.

response.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
response.text: The minority must obey the majority, right? This is how the world works.

response.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
response.text: What the... Seriously? Why did I even come to you for help? Darn it... Hey, Trendy Flyer, I'll let you win this time, but...

response.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
response.text: Listen up, girl! Go tell your brother to get in touch with us immediately if he doesn't want to bite it, you hear me?

response.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
response.text: Goodbye, my new voter friends. Bye, Blanche. Oh, and, if it's possible, please ask your brother to contact us. Thanks.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, they're finally gone. Those two are so weird. Oh, are you okay, kid?

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: I—I'm fine... Thank you... and that floating miss over there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Call me Paimon! This is {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: Th—Thank you... I am Blanche. You two must be great adventurers, then? I... I'll definitely visit the Adventurers' Guild to thank you!

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: But I have more important things to do right now... My brother's gone missing. I need to find him, but once I do, I will go visit you at the Adventurers' Guild!

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: So... Sorry, I need to go. Thank you again!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, wait up! Oh... She's gone... Why is she in such a hurry?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, let's help her. It's too dangerous for a kid to be out there alone. What if she can't find her brother?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: She doesn't seem to want to involve us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Must be because she doesn't have money... She knows hiring adventurers costs a lot of Mora. But those guys won't let her off the hook this easily... So we have to help!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, how about Paimon pays your fee? You can take it from Paimon's food fund!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And have you asked the food fund first?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: P—Paimon did...! It said... said, "Please use me how you see fit!"

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I don't remember ever saying that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! You're not Paimon's food fund... Well, you're not just that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon will fund your food supply once she gets rich! But first, let's stop making jokes... The girl needs our help!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Alright. Staying loyal to your friends is how the world works, after all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe. Paimon knew it. You were already planning to help, weren't you? Let's hurry up and catch up to her before she gets too far away!

choices.text: Or should we let our fists do the talking?
#Quit pestering me, or it's no more {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} Nice Traveler for you.

talks.objective: Catch up with the little girl, Blanche

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there, kiddo! Why are you sitting here?

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: #You're the ones from before... {NICKNAME} and Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Heheh. Good memory. We're here to help you find your brother!

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: Th—Thank you... but I'm worried that...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry! We won't charge you. We just can't stand idly by when someone needs our help!

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: It's not that... My brother left me some money. I'm just worried that...

choices.text: Are you worried about your brother being a Treasure Hoarder?

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: Yes...

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: You're good people. I can see that... But my brother and those two were... friends.

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: I know being a Treasure Hoarder isn't an honest job... I don't want to drag you into their business...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I know how you feel. I'm also looking for my family.

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: Huh?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's why finding your brother should be our first priority.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup! We'll find your brother first, and then we'll ask him what happened! See? There's nothing to worry about! We're the ideal people to help you! Just leave it to us!

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME} and Paimon... Y—You really are different. I see... Then, thank you for the help... Here's what happened...

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: A month or so ago, my brother happened to acquire a potion formula that could be very valuable. It's said to be the work of the Fontaine Research Institute, and is known as Pure Water.

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: After the Institute exploded, many things were scattered in the wilderness, and my brother often roamed around that area. That's how he picked it up.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: He came across it by himself?

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: No... Maybe... He might've been with a group of people... But my brother must've kept it for himself...

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: And that's why his friends called him a traitor... That's the only reason I can come up with, anyway...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No wonder those two Treasure Hoarders were looking for him... But why are all of you here? Are there any leads here?

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: Well, this used to be the backyard of the Fontaine Research Institute, which was home to various plant nurseries. It's said that the potioneer who created the Pure Water once lived here in seclusion to work on it.

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: The formula was written without too much detail or context, and contained the names of some raw ingredients... but my brother couldn't understand them, so he came here looking to see if there were any relevant manuscripts left...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And then he disappeared?

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: Yeah... From the look of this place, it's been long abandoned, with no nurseries in sight. Even this house is empty... Where could my brother have gone...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry, we'll find him. Oh, speaking of which, what's your brother's name, Blanche?

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: I—It's "Tricky Bulle Fruit." He's also one of the Fruity Order's operatives.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? That name's... a bit of a surprise... but not really... Anyway, let's try calling out to him from around here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Tricky Bulle Fruit! Where are you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Tricky Bulle Fruit! Your sister is looking for you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Tricky Bulle Fruit! Squeak if you can hear us!

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: S—Stop that Ms. Paimon... We might draw the attention of his enemies...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: M—Makes sense... Sorry! Paimon forgot that we're not the only ones looking for him.
Squeak!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What was that? Did you hear that? Paimon heard something!

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: I heard it!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Me too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's look around. Paimon's certain someone's hiding nearby!

choices.text: Are you worried that we might be Treasure Hoarders?

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: No, you can't be...

talks.objective: Look for where the suspicious voice is coming from

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Hello? Did someone say something? Are you hiding inside? Uh...
Doesn't seem like it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, Paimon thinks so too. Seriously... Wait! Y—Y—You... Who are you!? You said something again!

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: Brother!? It's my brother's voice! Brother? Are you inside?
I'm not anyone's brother. I just borrowed that guy's voice.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!? You're Tricky Bulle Fruit, aren't you!? Stop this act, right now! Your sister's worried to death!
I told you, it's not me. Come inside and you'll understand.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Try opening the door.)

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You push the door, but the door pushes back. You were hoping that it would open its heart to you, but the lock rejected you.
It's not gonna squeak open! It won't open, squeak~!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Stop acting like a kid! Just hand us the key already!
Doors come in all shapes and sizes, those that can open have a key, and those that can't go without, just like the situation you're facing right now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Shall I show you how violence opens all doors?
The poor world gave birth to a poor child, and the poor child has learned poor skills...
Violence, destruction, conflict... They shall have exceptionally poor effect on me.

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: Brother... No... My brother wouldn't say such things. You're not my brother! Who are you?
Oh, who's this? What a pure little princess! Ah, even the Bluecrown Finch would dance for you.
Allow me to introduce myself. I'm an apostle of the World of Intense Purity.
I've descended into this darn cabin now, so just call me the Cabin of Intense Purity.

dialogues.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
dialogues.text: As for your brother, that vile man known as Tricky Bulle Fruit, his vileness is beyond your ken.

dialogues.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
dialogues.text: And upon entering a pure world, the vile one found no escape.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sorry, a what world, again? What are you talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: My brother isn't that kind of person... Wait, he's gone to another world? Do you mean... he's dead?

dialogues.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
dialogues.text: The world has wrapped itself around him, just like resin wraps around a worm. He's merely trapped.

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: D—Does another world really exist?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #What do you think, {NICKNAME}? Do you believe that? You know better than us when it comes to other worlds.

choices.text: It's possible.

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: U—Um... Mr. Cabin of Intense Purity, please tell me how I can get my brother back from that world.

response.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
response.text: I merely know how to lead people there, but I don't know how to guide someone back.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: In that case, what's your objective?

response.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
response.text: Countless are the wise, but you are the rarest amongst them. I spoke in haste when there were more important things to do.

response.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
response.text: The person is trapped by the world, and the world is infected by that person, and thus has the pure white path fallen into darkness.

response.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
response.text: Therefore, I cannot embark on the road back home, and instead, require your assistance.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... Paimon didn't think the guy we were looking for was such a big troublemaker...

response.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
response.text: But do not forget that to help me is to help yourselves. Once everything is done, I shall "accidentally" leave a "key" behind...

response.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
response.text: And you shall unexpectedly obtain said "key"... due to blind chance, of course.

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: Will that allow me to bring my brother back?

response.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
response.text: I dare not guarantee your success, but this is the only way to the other side.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? You can't even guarantee that? Can you at least tell us how we're supposed to help you, then? And no bad stuff, we don't do that!

response.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
response.text: I swear in purity's name that I have never committed any evil, not from the moment of my birth.

response.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
response.text: I only require a few Pure Pinecones. They are all I need to repair the contaminated path.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Pure Pinecones? Paimon has never heard of those...

response.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
response.text: They are precious fruit planted by a potioneer, and can only be found around this cabin.

response.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
response.text: Why are they so effective, you ask? Why, they are miraculous herbs watered with Pure Water.

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: P—Pure Water!? Isn't that the potion formula my brother obtained!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now Paimon remembers. The potioneer of Fontaine Research Institute. Did he...

response.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
response.text: That previous potioneer is, indeed, the last lucky soul to have visited the World of Purity.

response.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
response.text: If we're talking about the fortune he obtained in that paradise, then it is this thing we call Pure Water. This cabin I now live in was once his residence.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! So others have been to that world too, have they?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon was a little skeptical about the truth of his words, but what he said matches what Blanche has told us. The cabin is where the potioneer used to live in seclusion...

response.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
response.text: I always speak the truth. No judge would ever accuse me of deceit.

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: #Now that we know my brother's whereabouts, I'll definitely find him. But Paimon, {NICKNAME}, I don't want to put you at risk...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Don't say things like that. We've already decided to help you, right, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: Well, in for one Mora, in for the lot...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe! Paimon knew you'd say that!

response.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
response.text: I see. In that case, could you please take this simple test of mine?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? A test? You didn't say anything about that! Don't you trust us!?

response.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
response.text: After seeing all of you, and especially after witnessing how valiant this blonde knight is, I took the liberty of inwardly labeling you as beyond question.

response.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
response.text: But to be honest, the Paradise of Purity is no children's playground. If you lack strength, your lives may be in danger.

response.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
response.text: If the princess ceases to be happy, then I shall never be happy either. So, please make a display of sufficient strength, dear knights.

response.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
response.text: It is a power that springs from purity, and it can control the purest source of water in the world. Thus, the people of this world call it the power of Hydro.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Water is just Hydro! That's nothing difficult for {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
response.text: I see you're willing to follow my plan. In that case, let us get straight to it!

response.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
response.text: Please observe these simple mechanisms carefully and light them up with the power of Hydro.

choices.text: An adventure to another world would be quite interesting.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe! That's our greatest adventurer for ya!

choices.text: Other worlds do exist.

dialogues.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
dialogues.text: Amazing, Golden Knight. The tiny machine didn't last a minute against you.

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: #You really are amazing, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: See? Paimon said there was nothing to worry about.

dialogues.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
dialogues.text: Then please find me Pure Pinecones. It's a miraculous fruit born of this place.

dialogues.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
dialogues.text: And please, do remember that I need a total of five.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, alright, we've got it. Seriously, why do we have to do something as trivial as searching for pinecones?

dialogues.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
dialogues.text: *sigh* I apologize, but I lack hands and feet. I'm just a pitiful, lowly little cabin.

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: Let's split up, Paimon. It'll speed things up. The sooner we find the pinecones, the sooner we'll get to see my brother. I'm heading off first, alright?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't go too far, Blanche! Don't leave our sight!

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: I know! I'll search over here on the east side.

dialogues.text: Don't push the blame on us! How could it be our problem? W—We're pure enough!

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: No! No! That's not what I mean. In the manuscript, that ingredient is known as the "power of water," so I thought it meant Hydro...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's why you wanted to test us with those Hydro mechanisms while you were disguised as the Cabin...

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: I'm embarrassed to say that there may be an error in my understanding... But what does the "power of water" represent? I must figure it out.

choices.text: Have you forgotten that you're still being hunted?

response.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
response.text: I know! Calla Lily never fails... But...

response.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
response.text: I cannot stop here. I must... I must finish it... I have no other choice...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't quite get you...

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: Isn't the "power of water" just the power of water?

response.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
response.text: The power of water? Only Hydro holds power, right? What other kind of power could water hold?

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: You've told me so many stories, brother, so you must know that in many stories, water itself is power.

response.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
response.text: Water itself?

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: That's right, just like the story about the potioneer which you told me when I was young.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The story about obtaining Pure Water from the World of Purity? But... wasn't that just a lie?

response.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
response.text: That's the only part I made up... The rest has been passed down by word of mouth for generations.

response.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
response.text: They say that there was once a handsome but eccentric young man in the Fontaine Research Institute, a prodigy in potions and alchemy.

response.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
response.text: But as the Institute's focus was not on potions and alchemy, and due also to his slightly withdrawn and narcissistic tendencies, he was somewhat ostracized.

response.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
response.text: Later on, he came to these mountains to live in seclusion and continue his research, and he invented many miraculous potions.

response.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
response.text: Unfortunately, none of them were preserved, because he poured them all into the ground.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He poured them all away!?

response.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
response.text: Yes, that's what the stories say, and that's why he's considered weird. Maybe all geniuses are like that?

response.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
response.text: But there was a turn of events later on, and some say that it was the work of the Hydro Archon, who couldn't bear to see those legendary potions just vanish.

response.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
response.text: As more and more potions were poured there, they gradually formed a small pond. The potioneer was so amazed by the pond's formation that he sat nearby and admired it all day.

response.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
response.text: No one knows if he was indulging in his own masterpiece or his own reflection in that masterpiece of his.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's so intriguing! What happened next?

response.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
response.text: After that, the young man would immerse himself in the pond all day. But one day, he accidentally slipped into the pond and drowned in his own creation.

response.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
response.text: Some time later, a little blue and white flower emerged from the center of the pond, its beauty rivaling that of the potioneer.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... That's such a sad story... Wait... <color=#00E1FFFF>A pond with a little flower</color>? Hasn't Paimon seen a place like that?

response.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
response.text: Are you serious? I mean, I didn't make this up, but it's still just a legend.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #But Paimon really has seen it before... Ugh, but she can't remember where! Do you remember, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: In the World of Intense Purity.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph! Guess you don't believe Paimon, huh? But she really has seen it, you know!

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: I—I know! We passed by a small pond like that while gathering the pinecones! There was a little flower at the center of the pond...

response.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
response.text: R—Really? That's just a story! Are you sure? I never noticed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You overlooked all of that because you were so focused on targeting us. That's why only Blanche remembers.

response.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
response.text: It seems I really... Sigh, forget it. Shall we head over and have a look? Perhaps the key to the "power of water" lies in that pond.

choices.text: I think I remember.
It's alright. We've accepted your apology.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's finally over. There were so many monsters! What attracted them?

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: They might have spawned here, which means that there might be some kind of wonderful power in this area.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: You see the little flower in the middle of the pond? It's... just like in the legends.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It doesn't look that different from an ordinary flower...

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: But the dew drops on it are so shiny! They're more beautiful than dew you find elsewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's collect some.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: Dew drops that have formed by absorbing essence... Maybe that's the truth behind the power of water?

talks.objective: Collect dew from the center of the pond

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: Stand back, Blanche!

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: I can feel the power within these dew drops just by looking at them. I have a strong feeling, now, that our next mixture will be a success. Let's go back and give it a try.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Great! 10,000 Mora now feels like 100,000!

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: I'll start mixing now. Just wait a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The orange-haired young man starts working in front of the console, and a smile of joy soon appears on his face.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: We've done it! We've done it! I don't even need to try it out. I just know! This is so much better than the rip-offs in the Fortress of Meropide!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoo! Our work finally paid off!

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: #Great! You're amazing! So are you, {NICKNAME}, Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, you contributed the most, Blanche.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: Yes, if she hadn't remembered the story and the pond...

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: That's nothing, brother. I remember everything you've ever said.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: Thank you, both of you, for not holding a grudge. I made two copies of the formula as I promised, as my apology.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nice, you kept your word. We'll gladly take it! That said, though, we only need one.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: And there's one for you, Blanche.

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: Why? You can just take some. It's not like I'm going anywhere, right?

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: No, we can't stay together forever. You have a bright future — that's not something you should waste here.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: Take the complete formula to the new Fontaine Research Institute. If they don't think it's important enough, then go somewhere further out.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: Go to the Akademiya in Sumeru, or Liyue, or even Mondstadt. Someone will appreciate it enough to take you in.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: You can be like other girls. You can get a good education in school. It's much better than listening to my tall tales.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that why you made the potion?

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: No, I've heard you say this stuff too many times! I'll go wherever you go!

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: Aren't you going to listen to your brother? Not anymore?

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: No, I don't! Not when you talk about this!

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: I don't want to get mad at you. Please, listen to me.

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: I hate it when you try to act like a big brother!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Blanche, come back! It's not safe around here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh boy, there she goes. Looks like you really made her mad this time.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: I don't want her to become just like me... I don't want her to become a Treasure Hoarder! She'll... understand one day.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Either way, we have to find her. It's too dangerous out there.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: Can I trouble you again to help me find her? I can only trust the two of you with this...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: She's family, isn't she? Why don't you do it yourself?

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: I... I still need to wrap this potion stuff up...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Still thinking about your blasted potions, huh? Bah. Paimon's got nothing to say to you. {NICKNAME}, let's go find Blanche.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There you are.

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: #*sob* {NICKNAME}, Paimon... He's trying to kick me out again...!

choices.text: He's not.

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: Why isn't he here, then?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well...

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: He must be upset that I'm always so clingy. But I just want to be with him. What's wrong with that?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, he's doing this because he loves you. Don't you think he must really regret becoming a Treasure Hoarder?

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: But I don't mind! He was already a Treasure Hoarder when he found me!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: When he found you?

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: He said he saw me crying on the side of the road when he was out scavenging one day, so he took me in. That was before I could speak and remember things.

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: In that case, can't I just become a Treasure Hoarder, too? Why won't he let me? He's so full of himself!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A Treasure Hoarder... Well... Maybe...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Anyway, let's go back first so he can stop fretting.

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: But he's not going to change his mind, is he?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We'll talk to him. You're his family. Paimon's sure you can work something out.

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: I guess so. Thank you both... But please, you have to help me convince him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry, we will. Wait, do you hear something?

response.speaker: Distant Male Voice
response.text: Calla Lily... I must die, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh no! It's Ruthless Calla Lily!

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: That's my brother!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We have to save him!

response.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
response.text: I didn't think the boss would send you, Calla Lily.

response.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
response.text: Well, I didn't think you would betray us either, Bulle Fruit.

response.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
response.text: There are things that I must do...

response.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
response.text: The little brat you found, I presume?

response.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
response.text: How... did you know?

response.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
response.text: I've had countless chances to make my move, but I don't kill anyone before I figure out what's going on. Well, now I know everything.

response.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
response.text: So I must die, right?

response.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
response.text: It's good that you're ready to pay the price. You did betray the organization for her sake, after all.

response.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
response.text: Actually, I have something to say. Bulle Fruit made a mistake, sure, but shouldn't we take a vote on this?

response.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
response.text: We should have had a share in the formula that he took. That means we should have a say in this, right?

response.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
response.text: As such, I propose we put the decision to kill Bulle Fruit to a vote. After all, the minority must obey the majority, right? Isn't that how the world works?

response.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
response.text: Wolfhook! Say something! Don't you live by that rule?

response.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
response.text: Why are you so afraid of her? We're all Operatives, aren't we?

response.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
response.text: Having Wolfhook stall me... You may as well have asked a sheep to stop a wolf. Is your New Tide just tomfoolery, Zaytun Peach?

response.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
response.text: Hey, leave the New Tide out of this.

response.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
response.text: The Fruity Order exists to maintain order in the world! We must not skip the vote!

response.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
response.text: There's no need to vote.

response.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
response.text: Seriously? Did she beat you silly?

response.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
response.text: I think Wolfhook understands that my presence represents the opinions of the boss and the rest of the group.

response.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
response.text: Even if the three of us are opposed, it's three against several dozen. And yes, in a perfect world, the minority must obey the majority.

response.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
response.text: But there is one more thing, Calla Lily.

response.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
response.text: Hmm?

response.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
response.text: I've always treated everyone in the Order like family. Even Bulle Fruit. Even you.

response.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
response.text: Families do not watch one another die, whether at the hands of outsiders or one of our own.

response.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
response.text: Do you mean to say that you're abandoning your own principles?

response.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
response.text: What I'm saying is that when it comes to family, it doesn't matter who's the majority and the minority!

response.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
response.text: Looks like I went too easy on you back when you pathetically begged for your life.

response.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
response.text: I'll do whatever it takes to stay alive. But now that there are three of us, we might stand a chance.

response.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
response.text: Too cool, brother! Too cool! Is this your latest principle?

response.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
response.text: No, Bulle Fruit taught me about this. I've just never applied it until today.

response.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
response.text: So another one wants to die. Well, Zaytun Peach? Are you sure? Do you really want to betray the boss?

response.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
response.text: Stop trying to put words in my mouth! I'll explain this to the boss myself. By the way, I'm tired of your arrogance!

response.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
response.text: Also, why don't you think about your name for a moment? Is it a fruit? Are Calla Lilies fruits?

response.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
response.text: I don't even know how you managed to become one of us. In fact, you're the real traitor! You've betrayed us simply by having that name!

response.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
response.text: I'm gonna show you what for today!

response.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
response.text: I see that you don't want to live, either. Fine. The Order's cleanup starts today!

response.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
response.text: Zaytun Peach, Wolfhook, I'm happy that you still consider me family.

response.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
response.text: But... I've been a crook my whole life, and this might be my last day in this world, so please, just let me do the right thing for once.

response.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
response.text: Stay out of it. This is my problem, and I should deal with it by myself. That way, the boss won't give you any trouble, either.

response.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
response.text: Are you out of your mind? This is not the time to try to be cool!

response.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
response.text: Don't worry, I've replicated the Pure Water, so I might stand a chance.

response.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
response.text: If that's really what you want, then I'll... support you...

response.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
response.text: Sounds great. If I don't come back, please take care of my sister for me.

response.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
response.text: Let's see what you've got.

choices.text: He just wants you to live a better life.

talks.objective: Go toward where the sound is coming from

dialogues.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
dialogues.text: It's my loss...

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: Wait! Is this for real? How is she so weak? Did my scolding affect her mentally or something? Am I even that amazing?

dialogues.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
dialogues.text: It is strange. She was way stronger back when she attacked me, but even a child could fight her right now...

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: Tell me the truth, Calla Lily! Is my potion too strong, or are you just going easy on us?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Isn't this because of {NICKNAME}'s help?

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: Even if we consider that, something still doesn't feel right...

dialogues.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
dialogues.text: A loss is a loss. I accept my defeat.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: You...

dialogues.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
dialogues.text: The boss won't come for you anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: R—Really?

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: That's how the boss works. I may not like Calla Lily, but if the boss sent her, then the boss won't pursue the matter no matter the outcome.

dialogues.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
dialogues.text: The Calla Lily who never fails has failed. Guess we're pretty good, huh? Brother.

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: Yeah, yeah, you're the best, if that's what you want! Either way, you'd better figure out how we're gonna explain this to the boss. Calla Lily is definitely going to tell on us.

dialogues.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
dialogues.text: Hurry up and ask your New Tide for solutions, then! I've been counting on it from the beginning, you know?

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: What New Tide? I've never even seen the New Tide! Stop being a kid! Forget it! Let's think about it after we get back.

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: No matter how great she is, she only has a single mouth, but we have two! It's two against one! One is completely useless when it's two against one!

dialogues.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
dialogues.text: Hmph. Naive idiots. I'm leaving.

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: Wait, Calla Lily, Zaytun Peach, Wolfhook. I have something for you.

dialogues.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: This is the formula for Pure Water that my brother deciphered. This belongs to all of you too...

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: He wronged all of you, so allow me to apologize on his behalf. I hope you can forgive him. He only did it for my sake.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: Sis...

dialogues.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
dialogues.text: ...I see.

dialogues.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
dialogues.text: Listen to your brother from now on, girl.

dialogues.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
dialogues.text: If I had a brother too, I might not have turned out this way.

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: Time to go. Take care of your sister, Crappy Bulle Fruit.

dialogues.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
dialogues.text: See you, Blanche. Bye, Bulle Fruit. And goodbye to the two of you too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's finally over, right? Phew!

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: No, there's still my sister...

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: No! I don't want to talk about that...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You've got to talk, even if you're siblings.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #C'mon, you two! {NICKNAME} is right! It's always super important to talk stuff out!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We have long conversations every day, too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon's gotta touch base with her food fund, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Just... let Paimon have this, would you?

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: Th—Then... Alright. I'll consider what my brother has to say... but I just... I just don't want to be separated from him.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You won't truly be apart.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: Indeed, we'll never truly be apart. It's just that you will experience many things while growing up, and we've all got to learn to live independently.

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: F—Fine, but then, you've gotta teach me...

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: Of course. I'll stay with you until you can stand on your own two feet.

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: It's a deal, then!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright! So what do you plan to do now?

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: I haven't figured that out yet. Anyway, Step One is to send a copy of the formula to the new Fontaine Research Institute. It can be considered their inheritance, after all. Haha!

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: I might try my luck at the Fortress of Meropide after that. Pure Water sells quite well over there. I mean, regardless of what Blanche decides to do, one simply can't do without Mora.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: The clock's ticking. It's time for us to leave.

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: #Are we in that much of a hurry? I wanted to cook for {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's alright, we'll meet again.

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: A—Alright. If you're too busy, I'll write to the Adventurers' Guild, so don't forget to pick it up!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We will! Safe travels!

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: #Farewell, {NICKNAME}! See you, Paimon! And safe travels to you too!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew! Gotta say, Paimon does feel a bit sad to see 'em go, but we've done something very meaningful, huh? Paimon's suddenly filled with confidence toward our future journeys, in fact.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What sort of confidence?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You thought of your family just now, right? It was written all over your face.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #You'll definitely find {M#her}{F#him}, and that's what Paimon's confident in! You should have confidence in it too!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #When we see {M#her}{F#him}, Paimon will help you talk {M#her}{F#him} around. After all, {M#she}{F#he} only has a single mouth, but we have two! It's two against one!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Remember, New Tide said that one is completely useless when it's two against one!

choices.text: Don't pick up that nonsense.

response.text: Nonsense? Paimon's just cheering you on!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, take this. It's Paimon's food funds! Paimon promised to pay the commission fees, remember? Hehe, Paimon's super trustworthy, huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's with that expression? Too embarrassed to say "thank you, Paimon"? That's gotta be it! Paimon heard it, though! That's right, you said "thank you, Paimon" in your heart, didn't you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And which case, "you're welcome"! Just don't forget to put more Mora in our food fund from now on, alright?

choices.text: You truly are the Trendy Flyer.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Trendy Flyer? Paimon's cheering you on, c'mon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Oh! Are you talking about those Hydro mechanisms at the entrance? Hehe, {NICKNAME} cleared that a long time ago.

dialogues.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
dialogues.text: Ah, you truly are excellent, Golden Knight. In that case, I'll get straight to the point.

dialogues.speaker: Cabin of Intense Purity
dialogues.text: Please find me Pure Pinecones. It's a miraculous fruit born of this world.

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: I've found one! We can do this!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cabin! Hey, Cabin! We have your Pure Pinecones!

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: Mr. Cabin, are you there?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Knock the door.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's strange... Why isn't it responding? That guy didn't just leave on his own, right!?

dialogues.speaker: Crucible of Intense Purity
dialogues.text: Huh? Hurry, over here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? That sounded like it came from behind the cabin...

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Her legs! Go for the legs!

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Calla Lily! Over here! C'mon, it's me you want! Over here!

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Go for her head! Come on! The head!

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Freeze her! Nice!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They should be placed here.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: I can feel the power within these dew drops just by looking at them. I have a strong feeling, now, that our next mixture will be a success. Let's go back and give it a try.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Great! 10,000 Mora now feels like 100,000!

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: I'll start mixing now. Just wait a moment.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: We've done it! We've done it! I don't even need to try it out. I just know! This is so much better than the rip-offs in the Fortress of Meropide!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoo! Our work finally paid off!

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: #Great! You're amazing! So are you, {NICKNAME}, Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, you contributed the most, Blanche.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: Yes, if she hadn't remembered the story and the pond...

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: That's nothing, I remember everything you've ever said.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: Thank you, both of you, for not holding a grudge. I made two copies of the formula as I promised, as my apology.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nice, you kept your word. We'll gladly take it! That said, though, we only need one.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: And there's one for you, Blanche.

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: Why? You can just take some. It's not like I'm going anywhere, right?

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: No, we can't stay together forever. You have a bright future — that's not something you should waste here.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: Take the complete formula to the new Fontaine Research Institute. If they don't think it's important enough, then go somewhere further out.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: Go to the Akademiya in Sumeru, or Liyue, or even Mondstadt. Someone will appreciate it enough to take you in.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: You can be like other girls. You can get a good education in school. It's much better than listening to my tall tales.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that why you made the potion?

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: No, I've heard you say this stuff too many times! I'll go wherever you go!

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: Aren't you going to listen to your brother? Not anymore?

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: No, I don't! Not when you talk about this!

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: I don't want to get mad at you. Please, listen to me.

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: I hate it when you try to act like a big brother!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Blanche, come back! It's not safe around here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh boy, there she goes. Looks like you really made her mad this time.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: I don't want her to become just like me... I don't want her to become a Treasure Hoarder! She'll... understand one day.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Either way, we have to find her. It's too dangerous out there.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: Can I trouble you again to help me find her? I can only trust the two of you with this...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: She's family, isn't she? Why don't you do it yourself?

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: I... I still need to wrap this potion stuff up...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Still thinking about your blasted potions, huh? Bah. Paimon's got nothing to say to you. {NICKNAME}, let's go find Blanche.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There you are.

dialogues.speaker: Blanche
dialogues.text: #*sob* {NICKNAME}, Paimon... He's trying to kick me out again...!

choices.text: He's not.

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: Why isn't he here, then?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well...

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: He must be upset that I'm always so clingy. But I just want to be with him. What's wrong with that?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, he's doing this because he loves you. Don't you think he must really regret becoming a Treasure Hoarder?

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: But I don't mind! He was already a Treasure Hoarder when he found me!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: When he found you?

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: He said he saw me crying on the side of the road when he was out scavenging one day, so he took me in. That was before I could speak and remember things.

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: In that case, can't I just become a Treasure Hoarder, too? Why won't he let me? He's so full of himself!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A Treasure Hoarder... Well... Maybe...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Anyway, let's go back first so he can stop fretting.

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: But he's not going to change his mind, is he?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We'll talk to him. You're his family. Paimon's sure you can work something out.

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: I guess so. Thank you both... But please, you have to help me convince him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry, we will. Wait, do you hear something?

response.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
response.text: Calla Lily... I must die, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh no! It's Ruthless Calla Lily!

response.speaker: Blanche
response.text: That's my brother!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We have to save him!

choices.text: He just wants you to live a better life.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: I didn't think the boss would send you, Calla Lily.

dialogues.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
dialogues.text: Well, I didn't think you would betray us either, Bulle Fruit.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: There are things that I must do...

dialogues.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
dialogues.text: The little brat you found, I presume?

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: How... did you know?

dialogues.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
dialogues.text: I've had countless chances to make my move, but I don't kill anyone before I figure out what's going on. Well, now I know everything.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: So I must die, right?

dialogues.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
dialogues.text: It's good that you're ready to pay the price. You did betray the organization for her sake, after all.

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: Actually, I have something to say. Bulle Fruit made a mistake, sure, but shouldn't we take a vote on this?

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: We should have had a share in the formula that he took. That means we should have a say in this, right?

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: As such, I propose we put the decision to kill Bulle Fruit to a vote. After all, the minority must obey the majority, right? Isn't that how the world works?

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: Wolfhook! Say something! Don't you live by that rule?

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: Why are you so afraid of her? We're all Operatives, aren't we?

dialogues.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
dialogues.text: Having Wolfhook stall me... You may as well have asked a sheep to stop a wolf. Is your New Tide just tomfoolery, Zaytun Peach?

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: Hey, leave the New Tide out of this.

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: The Fruity Order exists to maintain order in the world! We must not skip the vote!

dialogues.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
dialogues.text: There's no need to vote.

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: Seriously? Did she beat you silly?

dialogues.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
dialogues.text: I think Wolfhook understands that my presence represents the opinions of the boss and the rest of the group.

dialogues.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
dialogues.text: Even if the three of us are opposed, it's three against several dozen. And yes, in a perfect world, the minority must obey the majority.

dialogues.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
dialogues.text: But there is one more thing, Calla Lily.

dialogues.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
dialogues.text: I've always treated everyone in the Order like family. Even Bulle Fruit. Even you.

dialogues.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
dialogues.text: Families do not watch one another die, whether at the hands of outsiders or one of our own.

dialogues.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
dialogues.text: Do you mean to say that you're abandoning your own principles?

dialogues.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
dialogues.text: What I'm saying is that when it comes to family, it doesn't matter who's the majority and the minority!

dialogues.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
dialogues.text: Looks like I went too easy on you back when you pathetically begged for your life.

dialogues.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
dialogues.text: I'll do whatever it takes to stay alive. But now that there are three of us, we might stand a chance.

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: Too cool, brother! Too cool! Is this your latest principle?

dialogues.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
dialogues.text: No, Bulle Fruit taught me about this. I've just never applied it until today.

dialogues.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
dialogues.text: So another one wants to die. Well, Zaytun Peach? Are you sure? Do you really want to betray the boss?

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: Stop trying to put words in my mouth! I'll explain this to the boss myself. By the way, I'm tired of your arrogance!

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: Also, why don't you think about your name for a moment? Is it a fruit? Are Calla Lilies fruits?

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: I don't even know how you managed to become one of us. In fact, you're the real traitor! You've betrayed us simply by having that name!

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: I'm gonna show you what for today!

dialogues.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
dialogues.text: I see that you don't want to live, either. Fine. The Order's cleanup starts today!

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: Zaytun Peach, Wolfhook, I'm happy that you still consider me family.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: But... I've been a crook my whole life, and this might be my last day in this world, so please, just let me do the right thing for once.

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: Stay out of it. This is my problem, and I should deal with it by myself. That way, the boss won't give you any trouble, either.

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: Are you out of your mind? This is not the time to try to be cool!

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I've replicated the Pure Water, so I might stand a chance.

dialogues.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
dialogues.text: If that's really what you want, then I'll... support you...

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: Sounds great. If I don't come back, please take care of my sister for me.

dialogues.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
dialogues.text: Let's see what you've got.

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: Her legs! Go for the legs!

dialogues.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
dialogues.text: Calla Lily! Over here! C'mon, it's me you want! Over here!

dialogues.speaker: "Trendy Zaytun Peach"
dialogues.text: Go for her head! Come on! The head!

dialogues.speaker: "Guileless Wolfhook"
dialogues.text: Freeze her! Nice!

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: Ah... The wind sure is howling today... Huh? What's that? Don't mind me, I'm just a tourist...

dialogues.speaker: "Tricky Bulle Fruit"
dialogues.text: Ah... The wind sure is howling today...
